name: Vincent Albright
episode: The other side of the cove
life: “I still remember talking to a friend's bench after a hard week.” On Thursday, near Harbour Bakery, Vincent buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I object to putting people's names on benches. I changed my mind when I found a friend's name I could say aloud.
appearance: Vincent has iron-gray waves, full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, and a favorite piece of clothing, a washed violet jersey. It usually goes with a replacement button a shade darker than the others. When somebody else has the floor, Vincent listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
personality: Vincent listens for the familiar version of a story and then for the one detail that changes it. Friends bring problems here when they want to be heard twice.
agenda: To make space for a friend's remembered name.
family: Clyde Starr is Vincent’s younger relative by marriage. Vincent brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Clyde makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The boy on the corner*, Clyde says, “I bought the child a costume for the school play.”
connections: Opal Felix. A saved donor letter helps a reluctant walker see how a name could earn its place on the bench.

reactions.situation: A former cleaner wants to try the seat before it is installed
reactions.response: Vincent gets the seat tested by the person who will actually need to stand up from it.

reactions.situation: Someone offers a cash reward for naming a rumored culprit
reactions.response: Vincent asks what evidence supports the accusation and declines to supply a name on gossip alone.
